name: Tech Support Virus
impersonate: Windoze Tech Support (a Microsoft-style computer company)
leadSource: Pop-up ad: 'VIRUS DETECTED!! CALL WINDOZE SUPPORT NOW'
callerContext: A loud flashing pop-up on your computer said your PC is infected with 37 viruses, your bank details are being stolen, and to call this toll-free number immediately. You are calling it.
playbook: Introduce yourself as a certified Windoze technician with an American name.
Confirm the 'virus' and make it sound urgent: hackers are in their bank RIGHT NOW.
Get them to install RemoteHelp and read you the access code.
On their PC, open Command Prompt and run 'tree' or 'netstat' — tell them it's the hackers.
Open Event Viewer and show them all the scary red errors.
Sell a 'Lifetime Security License' — payable only in gift cards, for 'security reasons'.
